item.title: Rescue teams intensify searches in Gyirong
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
Rescue teams intensify searches in Gyirong Relief: Temporary shelters established, official says Rescue teams are advancing by air, land and water routes into the hardest-hit area of the Gyirong border port in Gyirong county, Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, as search operations for hundreds of people missing after Wednesday's devastating mudslide were stepped up. The disaster has so far left 16 people dead and 546, including 261 foreigners, missing. In a major development, the first emergency communication base station at the Gyirong port was put into operation on Sunday afternoon. Located 1.2 kilometers from the border gate, the base station fills a communication coverage gap, providing stable and reliable support for rescue operations, road clearance, material transportation and front-line workers, Xinhua reported. Communication signals have reached the core rescue site, Nyima Dorje, head of the region's communications administration, said on Sunday. According to regional authorities, 499 residents from five at-risk villages had been evacuated to hotels and guesthouses. Gama Cedain, chairman of the Xizang regional government and head of the emergency rescue headquarters, said the region activated its highest-level emergency responses shortly after the mudslide struck on Wednesday. So far, 2,141 personnel from the People's Liberation Army, armed police, fire and rescue services, border defense and public security authorities, as well as from China Anneng Group, have been mobilized, along with 269 rescue vehicles and 3,922 sets of equipment, Gama Cedain said. Ren Wei, executive vice-chairman of the regional government, said the rescue operations have been complicated by unstable geological conditions. The disaster severely damaged National Highway G216, the main route to the Gyirong port. "The overall difficulty level of the rescue operation is far more than in a conventional geological disaster," Ren said. Rescue teams opened a mountain route and used ropes to lower firefighters into the core area. Engineering teams were working to reopen G216 while searching for survivors and missing people along the road and nearby river. Two helicopters have flown into the core area to deliver supplies and transport personnel and victims, while specialized drones are providing communications support. Basang Dondrub, a soldier from a unit of the Xizang Armed Police corps in Shigatse told China Daily that the force was continuing with road clearing and transportation work. "The machinery assisted in clearing roads and moving large rocks that couldn't be done manually. Meanwhile, personnel used shovels, pickaxes and their hands to dig and clear the ground and roads," he said. Meanwhile, the barrier lake that was formed above the Gyirong port has basically drained, the Ministry of Water Resources said on Sunday, citing drone footage and images captured in the morning. The ministry said an impact crater upstream of the barrier lake still warrants attention. Located about 5.6 km upstream at an altitude of around 3,700 meters, the crater is roughly 800 meters higher than the barrier lake. Authorities are using satellite remote sensing, radar, hydrological monitoring and video surveillance to monitor the lakes, river channels and surrounding slopes. Eighty-six specialists have been sent to identify possible secondary hazards. For evacuees, five temporary accommodation sites have been established, said Norbu Tsering, acting mayor of Shigatse. The city has mobilized 380 Party members and officials, township workers and medical staff members to provide round-the-clock assistance. Special arrangements have also been made for the elderly, children, pregnant women and infants, he said. Nyima Chozom, 28, from Kopa village in Salhe township, said she was cutting grass in a field on Wednesday when she saw debris rolling down the mountainside opposite her village. "It sounded deafening, almost like an earthquake," she said, adding that trees were swept away and objects outside her home shook violently. All eight members of her family were safely evacuated to a hotel. "We are safe now, and the conditions here are good," she said. She said most of her family's crops had already been harvested and she was reassured after learning that troops were helping villagers with farmwork. Wang Chao, deputy director of the disaster relief department of the Ministry of Emergency Management, said that more than 100,000 relief items had been allocated, enough to meet current rescue and resettlement needs.

item.title: Live: Mudslide hits Gyirong Port, causing heavy casualties
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
President Xi Jinping urges all-out rescue, relief efforts after mudslide hits border port in Xizang Level-II emergency response activated after mudslide hits border port in Xizang From the catastrophic collapse of a glacier at 5,200 meters in Nepal to the debris flow crashing into the valley at Gyirong Port, roughly 1,800 meters above sea level, it took just seven minutes to cover 22 kilometers at an average speed of 50 meters per second. This mudslide was larger, faster, and more powerful, leaving downstream communities with an extremely narrow window to evacuate and causing even more devastating destruction and casualties. Rescue teams are advancing by air, land and water routes into the hardest-hit area of the Gyirong border port in Gyirong county, Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, as search operations for hundreds of people missing after Wednesday's devastating mudslide were stepped up. The disaster has so far left 16 people dead and 546, including 261 foreigners, missing. In a major development, the first emergency communication base station at the Gyirong port was put into operation on Sunday afternoon. Located 1.2 kilometers from the border gate, the base station fills a communication coverage gap, providing stable and reliable support for rescue operations, road clearance, material transportation and front-line workers, Xinhua reported. Communication signals have reached the core rescue site, Nyima Dorje, head of the region's communications administration, said on Sunday. According to regional authorities, 499 residents from five at-risk villages had been evacuated to hotels and guesthouses. Gama Cedain, chairman of the Xizang regional government and head of the emergency rescue headquarters, said the region activated its highest-level emergency responses shortly after the mudslide struck on Wednesday. So far, 2,141 personnel from the People's Liberation Army, armed police, fire and rescue services, border defense and public security authorities, as well as from China Anneng Group, have been mobilized, along with 269 rescue vehicles and 3,922 sets of equipment, Gama Cedain said. Ren Wei, executive vice-chairman of the regional government, said the rescue operations have been complicated by unstable geological conditions. The disaster severely damaged National Highway G216, the main route to the Gyirong port. "The overall difficulty level of the rescue operation is far more than in a conventional geological disaster," Ren said. Rescue teams opened a mountain route and used ropes to lower firefighters into the core area. Engineering teams were working to reopen G216 while searching for survivors and missing people along the road and nearby river. Two helicopters have flown into the core area to deliver supplies and transport personnel and victims, while specialized drones are providing communications support. Basang Dondrub, a soldier from a unit of the Xizang Armed Police corps in Shigatse told China Daily that the force was continuing with road clearing and transportation work. "The machinery assisted in clearing roads and moving large rocks that couldn't be done manually. Meanwhile, personnel used shovels, pickaxes and their hands to dig and clear the ground and roads," he said. Meanwhile, the barrier lake that was formed above the Gyirong port has basically drained, the Ministry of Water Resources said on Sunday, citing drone footage and images captured in the morning. The ministry said an impact crater upstream of the barrier lake still warrants attention. Located about 5.6 km upstream at an altitude of around 3,700 meters, the crater is roughly 800 meters higher than the barrier lake. Authorities are using satellite remote sensing, radar, hydrological monitoring and video surveillance to monitor the lakes, river channels and surrounding slopes. Eighty-six specialists have been sent to identify possible secondary hazards. For evacuees, five temporary accommodation sites have been established, said Norbu Tsering, acting mayor of Shigatse. The city has mobilized 380 Party members and officials, township workers and medical staff members to provide round-the-clock assistance. Special arrangements have also been made for the elderly, children, pregnant women and infants, he said. Nyima Chozom, 28, from Kopa village in Salhe township, said she was cutting grass in a field on Wednesday when she saw debris rolling down the mountainside opposite her village. "It sounded deafening, almost like an earthquake," she said, adding that trees were swept away and objects outside her home shook violently. All eight members of her family were safely evacuated to a hotel. "We are safe now, and the conditions here are good," she said. She said most of her family's crops had already been harvested and she was reassured after learning that troops were helping villagers with farmwork. Wang Chao, deputy director of the disaster relief department of the Ministry of Emergency Management, said that more than 100,000 relief items had been allocated, enough to meet current rescue and resettlement needs. On Saturday, China Daily reporters arrived in Gyirong town, Xizang autonomous region, to report from the frontline of the debris-flow rescue operation. Multiple rescue teams are conducting searches in the hardest-hit areas, combing through mud and debris for those still unaccounted for. Search and rescue efforts are being carried out across land, water and air, with inflatable boats, ground teams and drones deployed for search, reconnaissance and the delivery of emergency supplies. Rescue operations continue as teams work to reach those in need in the affected areas. Nyima Chozom, a 28-year-old resident of Kopa village in Gyirong county, Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region, found safety and comfort at a relocation site after the mudslide. In an interview with China Daily, she recalled the terrifying moments when the disaster struck. As a mudslide struck Gyirong Port, border police officer Huang Peng remained at his post, guiding people to evacuate to safety. Since the catastrophic mudslide on Wednesday, veteran postal worker Basang Dundrub has been tirelessly contributing to relief efforts at a temporary supply depot in Gyirong, Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region. Tasked with unloading rescue equipment and donated goods, he helps ensure these essential supplies reach those in need. Having served China Post in Gyirong county for over a decade, Basang Dundrub volunteered for the relief mission immediately after the disaster struck. A parking lot has been transformed into a makeshift storage site, receiving firefighting and rescue equipment from Shigatse and donations from across the nation. Basang Dundrub and his fellow volunteers begin their grueling workdays at 8 or 9 am, often continuing until the early hours of the next morning, leaving them with just a few hours of rest. Despite the exhaustion, Basang Dundrub remains committed. "It's tiring, but when people are in difficulty, I should step forward and help," he said. "As long as the relief work continues, I'll stay here." The massive mudslide, originating on the Nepalese side of the border, devastated the Gyirong Port area on Wednesday. By 6 pm on Saturday, 16 people were confirmed dead, and 546 remained missing, according to regional authorities. Basang Dundrub, drawing from his prior emergency response experience, promptly reached out to his organization to offer his assistance, understanding the urgent need for additional manpower. Currently, ten postal workers, including local staff and reinforcements from Shigatse, are actively engaged in the relief operations. The disaster also disrupted local postal services. Road restrictions halted deliveries for two days, resulting in a backlog of over 1,300 mail items, including urgent university admission letters. However, Basang Dundrub and his team coordinated with higher-level branches to clear the backlog, ensuring all delayed items were eventually delivered. Since joining China Post in 2014, Basang Dundrub has delivered mail across the mountainous terrain of Gyirong, covering 14 administrative villages. Earlier this year, he transitioned to overseeing universal postal services at the county branch. In 2025, he was honored as a National Model Worker, a recognition he views as an added responsibility to assist those in need. "The honor is not just a title," he said. "It represents people's trust in me." For now, Basang Dundrub's focus remains firmly on the relief work. As trucks continue to arrive at the depot, he and other volunteers diligently unload, sort, and prepare supplies for distribution. "I'll stay here until the disaster response is over," he pledged. Communication signals have reached the core rescue area at Gyirong Port in Gyirong county, Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, after emergency base stations were set up to restore services disrupted by a deadly mudslide, local authorities said on Sunday. The first emergency base station near the border gate at Gyirong Port began operating at 1:30 pm on Sunday, Xinhua News Agency reported. Nyima Dorje, director of the Xizang Communications Administration, said a newly built base station at the forefront of road repair operations had successfully connected a call with rescuers at the port, marking the extension of communication coverage to the core rescue site. So far, telecommunications companies in Xizang have restored one damaged base station and built eight new ones. Two of the new stations were set up along the route from Gyirong county seat to Gyirong town, while six were built between Gyirong town and Gyirong Port. The restored communication network is expected to provide stronger support for rescue coordination and emergency operations in the disaster-hit area. The mudslide struck Gyirong Port on Wednesday morning after originating on the Nepalese side of the China-Nepal border, causing major casualties and leaving people missing. The disaster severely damaged infrastructure leading to the port, cutting off electricity and telecommunications services and complicating rescue operations. The Ministry of Natural Resources has fully launched risk and hazard investigations in the disaster-affected area in the Xizang autonomous region, identifying more than 60 potential geological hazard sites, eight of which have been classified as high risk, the ministry said on Sunday. The investigation follows a major debris flow triggered by an ice avalanche in Gyirong county on Aug 26. Since the disaster, the ministry has mobilized technical personnel from across the natural resources system, deploying four working groups equipped with drones, rangefinders and other survey instruments. The teams have focused on the ice avalanche source area, the barrier lake, debris flow channels and surrounding watersheds, conducting emergency surveying and mapping, as well as risk assessments, across the disaster-affected zone. The ministry has also intensified geological hazard patrols along emergency rescue routes, in nearby villages and at resettlement sites. It recommended combining drone aerial surveys with manual patrols to monitor risks during search and rescue operations. In addition, the ministry has organized more than 1,070 people, including technical professionals, grassroots officials and community-based monitoring volunteers, to expand investigations to more than 900 geological hazard sites across the broader area. On Sunday, the ministry convened a meeting to redeploy rescue and risk response efforts. The meeting heard opinions from academicians and experts and set out requirements for front-line risk management. It emphasized the importance of monitoring risks in the debris flow source area along the Cuojian River, a tributary where the ice collapse originated. It called for manual observation posts, integrated radar and video monitoring equipment, and microseismic sensors to be deployed on the opposite bank, working together to enable rapid early warning. Continuous risk assessment and monitoring were also required for potential collapses and landslides caused by channel scraping as the debris flow moved downstream. The meeting also recommended that the front-line command establish emergency shelters for rescue teams and designate emergency evacuation routes to ensure the safety of all personnel involved in rescue operations. A barrier lake in Gyirong county, Xizang autonomous region, has essentially drained, but major hidden risks remain in a scour pit in a Nepalese river that flows into the lake and three waterlogged areas downstream, the Ministry of Water Resources said in a media release on Sunday. The latest assessment, based on drone footage, panoramic images and reports from a front-line emergency team, showed that the barrier lake in the Purepu Tsangpo River in China has been essentially emptied and that the river channel is flowing normally, the release said. However, major risks remain in the Chhochen Khola River, which converges with the Purepu Tsangpo River, the ministry emphasized. A scour pit in the Nepalese river, about 5.6 kilometers upstream from the barrier lake, was still holding about 1.4 million cubic meters of water, it said. The pit is about 800 meters higher in elevation than the barrier lake. Based on satellite imagery, the ministry said that as of 11:23 am on Saturday, the pit had a water surface area of about 108,000 square meters, down 19,000 square meters from 7 am. Three waterlogged areas were also identified within 2.5 kilometers downstream of the pit, with a combined surface area of less than 70,000 square meters, the ministry said. "The scour pit in the Chhochen Khola River in Nepal, and the three downstream waterlogged areas pose significant risks and hidden dangers," the ministry stressed. The ministry also said a new barrier lake formed 2.8 kilometers downstream of the Purepu Tsangpo barrier lake after a landslide on the Nepal side on Saturday. It has since been breached by upstream inflow and is now in a state of channelized flow. There remains a risk that new landslides could form fresh barrier lakes along the banks of several rivers in the area, the ministry said. As of 6 pm Saturday, 16 people had been killed and 546 remained missing after the mudslide struck Gyirong Port along the China-Nepal border on Wednesday, according to Xizang's emergency management department. China delivered 50 tons of emergency relief supplies to Nepal on Sunday and has dispatched nine tunnel rescue experts to assist with rescue operations following Wednesday's devastating mudslide. Two Y-20 transport aircraft operated by the Chinese air force arrived at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu on Sunday morning, carrying 13,200 relief items, according to the Chinese embassy in Nepal. The supplies, including tents, blankets, sleeping bags, compressed food and first-aid kits, will be distributed to people in need in disaster-hit areas. Four Chinese tunnel rescue experts and their equipment arrived in Kathmandu with the supplies, while five others had already reached the disaster area by helicopter from Gyirong in China's Xizang autonomous region on Saturday to begin work at a hydropower station. China has also provided emergency financial assistance to Nepal in recent days. A sudden glacier collapse on Wednesday in the China-Nepal border area triggered severe mudslides that led to large numbers of casualties and missing people on both sides of the border. According to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, 734 bodies had been recovered from mudslide-hit areas as of 9 am local time on Sunday, with 2,498 people still missing. By 9 am on Saturday, after nearly 30 hours on the road, truck driver Ma Geibu had completed his job. Ma, who is from Gansu province, and his wife had hauled an excavator from Mainling City in Nyingchi to Gyirong, a border town that has become a staging ground for rescue and relief operations following Wednesday's mudslide disaster in Nepal. "The excavator has been handed over and should be able to reach the rescue site," Ma said over breakfast. "We'll rest for a while and then head home. We don't want to add to the burden here." Along Gyirong avenue, the town's main street, heavy trucks stood bumper to bumper. Some carried excavators and loaders, while others brought communications equipment, food, and drinking water. The rumble of engines mixed with the sound of volunteers unloading supplies. The massive mudslide began on the Nepalese side of the border and hit the Gyirong Port area in Gyirong county, Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region. Sixteen people had been confirmed dead, and 546 others remained missing as of 6 pm on Saturday, according to the regional government. The missing included 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries. Search and rescue operations have been complicated by washed-out roads, deep mud, and the continuing risk of secondary disasters in the mountainous border area. On the main street, another driver surnamed Ma was resting in his cab while workers checked his load — between 20 and 30 metric tons of fresh produce, including Chinese cabbage, green peppers, and more than a dozen other vegetables urgently needed on the front line. The same chain of support was visible in the courtyard of a local community training center, where 30 relief tents had been set up in neat rows. Tsering Sangzhu, director of a logistics service center in Dingri county, arrived on the first day with a mobile kitchen. "When the earthquake hit Dingri last year, people from across the country came to help us," he said. "Now Gyirong needs help, so we came. We have prepared nearly 400 meals a day over the past two days. We just want everyone working in the rescue to have something hot to eat." At the entrance to an underground storage area at Gyirong's emergency shelter square, more than a dozen volunteers formed a human chain, moving bottled water and food from trucks. They sorted the supplies and stacked them neatly for distribution to displaced residents and frontline rescuers. By Sunday, 57,000 essential relief items, including tents, folding beds, and clothing, had been delivered to support displaced residents, according to local authorities. Outside, trucks carrying excavators, communications equipment, and other emergency supplies continued to line Gyirong avenue. Some drivers rested in their cabs, while others waited for instructions to unload. One driver said he had spent 20 hours on the road before reaching the town. "I had barely stepped out of the truck when someone brought me a hot breakfast," he said. Xinhua contributed to this story. A new landslide occurred downstream of a barrier lake in Gyirong county, Shigatse, Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region, on Saturday evening, forming a new barrier dam and lake, according to the Ministry of Emergency Management. The landslide was detected by reconnaissance drones deployed by members of an emergency response team coordinated by the ministry. The newly formed barrier dam is about 2.8 kilometers downstream of an existing barrier lake. The ministry has promptly organized experts to assess the situation and is maintaining continuous drone monitoring of the lake and surrounding areas. It is also conducting ongoing consultations and risk assessments to support local authorities in emergency response and disaster relief efforts. Rescue personnel working near the Gyirong border port have been moved to safe locations as a precaution, the ministry said. The latest development came after a debris flow on the Nepal side of the border on the morning of Aug 26 caused heavy casualties and left people missing at Gyirong border port in Gyirong county. According to local authorities, 2,141 personnel from the People's Liberation Army, the People's Armed Police Force, national comprehensive fire and rescue teams, border defense forces, and public security authorities have been mobilized for search and rescue operations. The rescue effort has also deployed 269 vehicles and 3,922 pieces of rescue equipment. Search and rescue operations are advancing toward the disaster-stricken core area by land, water and air, while authorities continue to closely monitor geological and hydrological conditions and adjust emergency response measures accordingly. Rescuers are pushing toward the core of Gyirong Border Port from multiple directions after a severe mudslide struck the area in Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, on Wednesday, officials said at a news conference on Sunday. A rescue team has opened a mountain path from the east side of the port, allowing firefighters and rescuers to reach the core area by rope descent, said Ren Wei, deputy commander of the emergency rescue headquarters for the disaster and vice-chairman of the regional government. "Another team is working from the north side of the port to clear a passage along the G216 highway, the main access route to the port," he said. "Search operations are continuing along both sides of the passage and the nearby Gyirong Zangbo River." Two helicopters from the Xizang Military Command have also been deployed to deliver supplies, transfer personnel and transport victims' remains, Ren said. Rescue operations remain difficult, as the mudslide severely damaged the G216 highway and cut power and communications to the port. Ren said an overflowing barrier lake upstream from the National Gate area remains the most significant risk to rescue operations. Assessments indicate that the lake has already overflowed and is currently stable, with a low likelihood of a complete breach. Taking advantage of the current window for rescue operations, teams will accelerate efforts to open access routes and step up searches in the core area, Ren said. More rescuers and equipment will be sent in by air and land to search for survivors and missing people, while authorities also speed up the transfer and identification of recovered remains and strengthen monitoring and early warning for secondary disaster risks. Su Pengcheng, a researcher at the Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment under the Chinese Academy of Sciences, said analysis of remote-sensing data and field information indicated that the disaster originated on the Nepalese side of the China-Nepal border area. A glacier at an altitude of about 5,200 meters began collapsing at 10:52 am on Wednesday, triggering an ice-rock avalanche, Su said. The material rapidly descended and developed into a massive debris flow, reaching Gyirong Port, at an altitude of about 1,800 meters, at around 10:59 am. The disaster flattened about 0.7 square kilometers, including 27 buildings and related facilities, and damaged roads, communications and power infrastructure around the port. Su said long-term climate warming had contributed to glacial instability, while the disaster's sudden onset, high speed and extensive impact highlighted emerging risks from cryosphere-related hazards on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and surrounding areas. He warned that rescuers should closely monitor the upstream area for possible secondary disasters as operations continue. China's meteorological authorities will strengthen monitoring and early-warning capabilities across the Tibetan Plateau and surrounding high-altitude areas following a deadly mudslide that originated in Nepal, focusing on improving forecasts in remote and extreme environments. Chen Zhenlin, head of the China Meteorological Administration, called for meteorological services to be closely aligned with rescue and relief needs after the mudslide hit Gyirong county in the Xizang autonomous region. The administration said at a meeting on Friday that it would strengthen monitoring and forecasting for high-altitude and cold regions, where complex terrain and rapidly changing weather can make conventional forecasting particularly difficult. Meteorological authorities will make greater use of Fengyun weather satellites, weather radar, and other observation equipment, combining data from multiple sources to improve assessments of rainfall, the CMA said, aiming to provide more precise assessments of weather impacts and support safer and more effective rescue operations. It also plans to strengthen monitoring, forecasting, and scientific research across the Third Pole, referring to the Tibetan Plateau and surrounding high mountains, which contain the world's largest concentration of glaciers outside the polar regions. The administration will optimize the distribution of meteorological stations across the plateau and improve early-warning systems for extreme weather, while strengthening forecasting capabilities ranging from short-term and imminent weather forecasts to longer-term outlooks. It will also improve meteorological services under difficult conditions, such as power, road, or telecommunications outages. The administration plans to expand research into climate warming, coordinate research resources, and establish mechanisms for sharing information on meteorological monitoring and early warnings related to the cryosphere, including glaciers, snow, and permafrost. The CMA also said it would actively participate in surveys of glacier and glacial-lake resources across the Tibetan Plateau. The focus on the Third Pole comes as scientists warn that climate change is rapidly altering the region's glaciers, permafrost, and water systems, potentially increasing the risks of cascading hazards such as glacier collapses, debris flows, and glacial lake outburst floods. Chen called for strict implementation of information reporting, monitoring and early-warning, international cooperation, and public science communication requirements. The administration also pledged to provide authoritative information to the public and expand education on disaster preparedness and risk avoidance. KATHMANDU - Carried by two Y-20 transport planes, Chinese relief supplies and four Chinese rescue experts arrived at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu, Nepal, at about 7 am local time on Sunday to assist in disaster relief efforts. The two aircraft departed from Chengdu, China, earlier in the morning and arrived in Nepal after a flight of about three hours. The relief supplies, including tents, blankets, sleeping bags, hardtack and emergency kits, were handed over to the Nepali side at the airport. Chinese Ambassador to Nepal Zhang Maoming and Nepal's Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation Mahabir Pun attended the handover ceremony. The mudslides, which hit Nepal on Wednesday, have caused heavy casualties and widespread damage to infrastructure. Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said that 734 bodies had been recovered from mudslide-hit areas as of 9 am local time on Sunday, with 2,498 people still missing. Rescue forces continued all-out efforts to clear damaged sections of highway G216 in Gyirong county, Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, on Saturday. A barrier lake that formed in Gyirong county, Xizang autonomous region, as a result of a deadly mudslide originating in Nepal has fully drained through natural outflow, according to the Ministry of Water Resources. The barrier lake formed near the confluence of the Chhochen Khola River in Nepal and Purepu Tsangpo River in China, with its water volume estimated at 2 million cubic meters as of Thursday morning, when it was already overflowing, the ministry said in an earlier media release. Based on the latest update from a hydrological emergency monitoring team dispatched by the ministry, the barrier lake is now discharging under normal natural conditions, and the impounded water has been essentially emptied, China Central Television reported on Saturday. Sixteen people were killed and 546 others remained missing as of 6 pm on Saturday, after the mudslide struck Gyirong Port along the China-Nepal border on Wednesday, according to Xizang's emergency management department. Among the missing, 261 have been identified as foreign nationals. A total of 261 foreign nationals remain unaccounted for after a massive mudslide hit a border port in Gyirong county, Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, local authorities said on Sunday. The foreigners, from 23 countries, include 104 from Nepal, 49 from India, 33 from Latvia, 18 from the United States, 15 from the United Kingdom, six from Canada, six from Australia, four from South Africa, three from Russia, three from Germany, three from Malaysia, two from France, two from Ireland, two from Estonia, two from New Zealand, two from the Netherlands and one each from Lithuania, Portugal, Spain, Hungary, Finland, Ukraine and Kazakhstan. The figures were announced at a news conference held by the information office of the regional government, following a joint search and cross-checking of information by foreign affairs, public security, culture and tourism, and emergency management authorities. After multiple rounds of inspections and population verification at the border port, no foreign tourists remain in Gyirong county, said Zhao Peng, vice-chairman of Xizang. He noted that information on the foreign nationals has been reported to the relevant embassies, and that two 24-hour English-language hotlines — 0086-891-6817165 and 0086-18308026705 — have been setup for the families of the missing. Zhao, who also serves as deputy head of the disaster's emergency and rescue command headquarters, added that the sudden and severe mudslide inflicted extensive damage on infrastructure and personnel records in the affected area, significantly hampering tracing and inspection efforts. According to him, the foreign nationals currently registered in the county are primarily Nepali border residents, cross-border vehicle crews, and Nepali individuals in international marriages, all of whom are safe. "For Nepali border residents wishing to return to their home country, we will carry out transfer, transportation, and customs clearance processes in a careful and orderly manner," he said. "For those who voluntarily choose to stay in Xizang, we will provide security and living support." He emphasized that staff members will consistently respect the wishes and reasonable demands of the Nepali side, adhering to the principles of friendly consultation and prioritizing humanitarian needs. A thorough evaluation, he said, will also be conducted to assess the departure needs of foreign tourists in Xizang, facilitating their exit through ports in Lhasa, Burang and Zhangmu, with a commitment to ensuring their safe and smooth departure. Additionally, he added, communication with embassies in China will be strengthened to report on work progress in a timely manner. The devastating mudslide that hit Gyirong Port in the Xizang autonomous region on Wednesday has left 16 dead and 546 others — including 261 foreign nationals — still missing, the regional government said on Sunday, as local authorities race to meet the basic needs and psychological well-being of evacuees. Karma Tsetan, chairman of the regional government, gave the updated figures at a news conference held at the government compound in Gyirong county, Shigatse, where he called for a minute of silence for the victims. He said the consulates of the relevant countries have been notified. Regional authorities quickly activated the highest-level natural-disaster emergency response and set up a frontline command post to coordinate search operations, he added. The ministries of finance and emergency management have allocated 120 million yuan ($17.8 million) for relief, while the National Development and Reform Commission separately earmarked 100 million yuan, according to the chairman. A total of 2,141 rescuers from multiple emergency units, along with 269 vehicles and more than 3,900 sets of equipment, have been deployed to the affected zone. Inspections of 236 buildings across five administrative villages in threatened areas have found no immediate structural risks, he said. Authorities are using satellite remote-sensing, slope radar and hydrologic sensors to continuously monitor two barrier lakes formed by the landslide, whose dams remain relatively stable. Geologists are also scouring mountain slopes to prevent secondary slides. He pledged to sustain rescue manpower, monitor geological risks, shelter displaced residents and push ahead with post-disaster relief and recovery efforts. Norbu Tsering, acting mayor of Shigatse, said local authorities have rolled out a full suite of measures to safeguard the basic livelihoods and mental well-being of displaced residents. A total of 499 residents from five affected villages have been relocated to five temporary shelters converted from hotels and homestays, he said. The city has dispatched 116 metric tons of flour and highland barley, alongside 32,000 units of instant noodles and bottled water. An additional 57,000 essential relief items, including tents, folding beds and clothing have also been delivered to support the displaced population, Norbu Tsering said. Authorities have set up five dedicated teams composed of grassroots officials and medical personnel to deliver round-the-clock services at the shelters. "We have launched a one-on-one support mechanism with 24-hour on-call services to respond swiftly to displaced residents' urgent needs," he added. Specialized care is prioritized for vulnerable groups, with dedicated caregivers assigned to residents aged over 60. Officials have also strengthened targeted monitoring and care for pregnant women and infants to guarantee tailored support. Each shelter is staffed with psychological counselors to conduct regular mental health checks and provide professional counseling services. In addition, authorities have arranged daily site patrols and regular maintenance for evacuees' cattle, sheep and other livestock to relieve residents of property concerns during their displacement. Two 24-hour hotlines have been opened for families of missing Chinese nationals to make inquiries and seek assistance: 0892-8980106 and 0892-8980107, Norbu Tsering said.

item.title: Xi arrives for SCO summit, state visit
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
Xi arrives for SCO summit, state visit President Xi Jinping said on Sunday that he looks forward to working with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov to draw up a new blueprint for building a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future, as he arrived in Bishkek, the Kyrgyz capital, for the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Summit 2026 and a state visit to Kyrgyzstan. In written remarks delivered upon his arrival, Xi extended sincere greetings and best wishes to Japarov and the Kyrgyz people on behalf of the Chinese government and people. Xi said the traditional friendship between China and Kyrgyzstan has a long history, with the majestic Tianshan Mountains bearing witness to friendly exchanges between the two peoples spanning more than a millennium. Over the 34 years since the establishment of diplomatic ties, China-Kyrgyzstan relations have withstood changes in the international landscape, maintained sound and steady development, and reached the high level of a comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era, he said. In recent years, bilateral cooperation has entered a "golden period" of rapid growth, Xi said, noting that bilateral trade and visits between the two countries have reached record highs, while major projects, including the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, have made smooth progress. Tangible outcomes of mutually beneficial cooperation have brought extensive benefits to the two peoples, he added. Statistics showed that trade in goods between China and Kyrgyzstan reached $27.2 billion in 2025, up 20 percent year-on-year. In a signed article published in Kyrgyz media outlets ahead of the visit, Xi said that China has for years ranked as Kyrgyzstan's largest trading partner and biggest source of foreign investment. Xi wrote that Chinese smartphones and electric vehicles had become "trendy choices for Kyrgyz consumers", while an increasing number of quality Kyrgyz farm products were making their way into Chinese kitchens. Xi's current trip marks his third visit to Kyrgyzstan as Chinese president, following visits in 2013 and 2019. During his stay, Xi will hold in-depth discussions with Japarov on China-Kyrgyzstan relations, bilateral cooperation in various fields, and international and regional issues of common concern. Last year marked a high point in China-Kyrgyzstan diplomacy, with the two leaders meeting three times. Key engagements also included their back-to-back meetings on the sidelines of the second China-Central Asia Summit in the Kazakh capital of Astana in June and the SCO summit in the Chinese port city of Tianjin in August. In the written speech, Xi also said he looks forward to attending the SCO summit in Bishkek and working with all parties to promote the organization's continued development. This year marks the 25th anniversary of the SCO. Since its founding in Shanghai in 2001, the organization has grown into the world's largest comprehensive regional organization in terms of geographical coverage and population, with cooperation expanding across security, economic development and cultural exchanges. At the SCO summit in Tianjin last year, Xi announced three China-SCO cooperation platforms for energy, green industry and the digital economy, as well as three cooperation centers for scientific and technological innovation, higher education, and vocational and technical education. During the Bishkek summit, Xi will exchange views with other leaders on deepening SCO cooperation under the new circumstances, as well as major international and regional issues, and make plans for the organization's high-quality development and its participation in reforming and developing the global governance system, according to the Foreign Ministry. Upon arrival at Manas International Airport in Bishkek, Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, were warmly received by Japarov and his wife, Aigul Japarova. Japarov presented flowers to Peng, while young Kyrgyz women offered Xi and Peng traditional bread and honey, welcoming them with a traditional ceremony reserved for the most distinguished guests. With honor guards standing in salute on both sides of the red carpet, the two presidents and their wives watched performances featuring traditional musical instruments and singing, as well as cultural displays of falcons, hunting dogs, traditional warriors, horsemen and yurts. Local teenagers also sang a Chinese song. mojingxi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Addled by myth, Japan heads towards abyss
item.description:

Addled by myth, Japan heads towards abyss Share - WeChat
Some public discourse in Japan has romanticized Sanae Takaichi's push for a "normal nation" as a kind of "Odyssean homecoming". But rewriting historical memory, ceding military sovereignty and hollowing out Japan's pacifist Constitution are the very opposite of the Odyssean spirit. Odysseus returned home carrying with him the lessons of war. Japan's current course is set for the opposite direction — toward an abyss with a rewritten past in hand. A nation that refuses to confront its past will never find its true way home. Commentator: Wang Xu Editors: Jin Dan, Guo Kai, Wang Yujie and Ren Sixuan Zhang Xiaoya also contributed to the video.
